cases.text: The first element of a JavaScript array is at index zero.

triage.normalized_claim: The first element of a JavaScript array is at index zero.
search_queries: JavaScript array indexing start at zero

outcome.explanation: The source explicitly states JavaScript arrays are zero-indexed and the first element is at index 0.

evidence.excerpt: JavaScript arrays are zero-indexed: the first element of an array is at index 0, the second is at index 1, and so on — and the last element is at the value of the array's length property minus 1.

For the next community challenge, I chose a blue robot puzzle. The puzzle has a silver tower and a green bridge. The challenge is about the blue robot puzzle, not a racing game.
the next practice session is scheduled for tuesday at 7 in the evening. this is a fictional schedule for the automated test. tuesday at 7 is the time i said.
the word for the treasure hunt is pineapple. remember pineapple if you want to find this moment later. the treasure hunt word is not a password and does not grant access to anything.
my chosen color for the imaginary team shirt is cyan. the shirt has white stripes. if someone asks which color i chose for the shirt, the answer is cyan with white stripes.
the plan for the fictional cooking break is tomato soup and toasted bread. i chose tomato soup rather than a noodle dish. this is another memory search example.
I changed the target for the building challenge from 10 rooms to 12 rooms. The old target was 10. The current target in this scripted example is 12 rooms.
the imaginary robot has a nickname. its nickname is pocket comet. pocket comet carries a small orange backpack. this sentence gives the search engine a distinctive name to retrieve.
The practice route begins at the stone arch and finishes at the wooden bridge. The starting point is the stone arch. The finishing point is the wooden bridge.
halfway through this test, i promised to share the puzzle solution after the final round. i did not promise to share it before the round. the timing of the promise matters in this memory example.
the next drawing should contain three paper boats and one lighthouse. three paper boats and one lighthouse are the objects i selected. no other picture is being shown in this test.
For the imaginary picnic, I selected apples, pears, and sparkling water. The drink is sparkling water. This is a scripted list that the memory tool can retrieve from stored transcript segments.
I decided to call the next fictional level lantern garden. Lantern garden contains a pond and five stone steps. The name of the level is lantern garden.
The proposed break is five minutes long. I said five minutes, and then I said we would return to the puzzle. The break length is another number that can be searched as words or digits.
I put the imaginary spare key in the yellow toolbox. The toolbox is next to the workbench. This is a story prop in the test script, not a real credential or a real location.
the fictional score target is 42 points. 42 points is the target for the final round. the script does not say the target is 24 points.
The next paper model is a small observatory with a copper dome. I chose an observatory, not a castle. Its dome is copper in this scripted example.
the last community vote in this fictional story selected the forest path. the forest path won over the river path. these words are narration for a technical test rather than votes from real viewers.
this is the end of the pre-recorded stream memory test. the closing phrase is bring the receipts. the tool should quote stored speech and use the stored time rather than inventing either one.
